title: Production Containerization with Docker & .NET
description: Build hardened, lightweight, multi-stage Docker images for ASP.NET Core and React applications using chiseled and non-root containers.

data.text: Containers ensure reproducibility across development, staging, and production environments. However, creating naive Dockerfiles that compile code as root or package entire .NET SDKs into production images introduces severe CVE security vulnerabilities and inflates image sizes to over 1GB. Modern container engineering leverages multi-stage builds, layer caching, non-root user execution, and ultra-minimal chiseled images.
Production Multi-Stage Dockerfile for ASP.NET Core

The Dockerfile below utilizes Microsoft's official .NET chiseled runtime image (Ubuntu Chiseled)—which contains zero package managers, no shell (/bin/sh), and runs as an unprivileged non-root user, shrinking image size to under 110MB.

data.title: Hardened Multi-Stage Dockerfile for .NET Web API
data.content: Leverages separate build, publish, and chiseled runtime stages for maximum security:
data.code:
# Stage 1: Build & Restore with layer caching
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Copy csproj files first to maximize Docker layer cache hits
COPY ["src/LearnAI.Api/LearnAI.Api.csproj", "src/LearnAI.Api/"]
COPY ["src/LearnAI.Core/LearnAI.Core.csproj", "src/LearnAI.Core/"]
RUN dotnet restore "src/LearnAI.Api/LearnAI.Api.csproj"

# Copy remainder of source code and build
COPY . .
WORKDIR "/src/src/LearnAI.Api"
RUN dotnet build "LearnAI.Api.csproj" -c Release -o /app/build

# Stage 2: Publish optimized binaries
FROM build AS publish
RUN dotnet publish "LearnAI.Api.csproj" -c Release -o /app/publish \
    --no-restore \
    /p:UseAppHost=false

# Stage 3: Minimal Chiseled Runtime (No shell, non-root app user)
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:9.0-noble-chiseled AS final
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 8080
ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080
ENV DOTNET_EnableDiagnostics=0

# Copy published binaries
COPY --from=publish /app/publish .

# Container runs as unprivileged 'app' user automatically
USER app
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "LearnAI.Api.dll"]

data.text: Container Best Practices for AI Microservices

items.hint: Copy only .csproj files before running dotnet restore so dependencies are cached between code edits.
Never run container workloads as root; use USER app to prevent privilege escalation attacks.
Remove bash, curl, and package managers from runtime images to eliminate attack tools.
Implement /healthz liveness and readiness endpoints in ASP.NET Core for orchestrator probing.
Inject AI service endpoints and secrets dynamically at container launch; never bake keys into image layers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Multi-stage Docker builds separate heavy SDK build tools from lean runtime images
Chiseled Ubuntu images eliminate shells and package managers, slashing attack surface and image size
Always run containers as unprivileged users (USER app) for zero-trust security
Structure Docker commands to maximize layer caching on dependency restoration
Pass secrets and configurations via environment variables or Kubernetes secrets, never baked in
data.takeaway: Hardened containerization provides a secure, minimal, and predictable foundation for deploying .NET AI services across Kubernetes, App Service, and Container Apps.
